# Helix

> Helix is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) and private alternative to GraphPad Prism for macOS. It organizes, analyzes and visualizes scientific data, from raw numbers to publication-ready graphs. Statistics are computed by R (through webR, R compiled to WebAssembly) and graphs by Plotly, entirely on the user's Mac.

Also called "Helix Data Analysis" or "Helix for Mac", to tell it apart from other software named Helix (such as the Helix text editor or Perforce Helix). Helix is made by mickaphd, a scientist in Paris, with the help of Claude Code. It requires macOS 13.3 (Ventura) or later and runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. It is signed and notarized by Apple.

Each table holds its own analyses and graphs, which update as soon as the data change.

- Tables: Column, XY (with replicates), Grouped, Multiple Variables, Contingency and Survival; copy and paste with Excel or Numbers; exclude values without deleting them; transform or normalize (logarithms, percent of control, z-scores) into a table that follows its own; notes and color tags.
- Analyses (guided assistants, computed by R): descriptive statistics, normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk), outliers (ROUT, Grubbs); unpaired, Welch, paired, ratio and lognormal t tests, Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, with effect sizes; one-way, Welch's and repeated-measures ANOVA, mixed-effects models, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman, multiple comparisons (Tukey, Dunnett, Šidák, Holm-Šidák, Fisher's LSD, Games-Howell, Dunn); two-way ANOVA (ordinary, repeated measures, Scheirer-Ray-Hare), multiple t tests; Pearson and Spearman correlation; linear, nonlinear (dose-response 3PL, 4PL, 5PL, growth, decay, Michaelis-Menten), logistic and multiple regression; standard curve interpolation; area under the curve; survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, hazard ratios, Cox regression); chi-square and Fisher's exact test with relative risk, odds ratio, sensitivity and specificity. Every result shows the data it analyzed, a plain-language summary and its assumptions checked.
- Graphs: individual values, box and violin plots, bars (including 100% stacked), lines, scatter plots, histograms, dose-response curves, Kaplan-Meier survival curves with the number at risk, heatmaps, pie charts, volcano plots, QQ and residual plots; significance stars, group letters and fitted curves from the analyses; log axes, 95% CI error bars, reference lines; your own palettes and heatmap gradients; Match gives a graph the look of another one; export as PNG at 150, 300 or 600 dpi, SVG or JPG.
- Privacy: no account, no cloud, no telemetry; the only connections are a daily check on GitHub for a newer version and the updates the user chooses to install. Helix updates itself after asking.
- Projects: several projects open at once, each in its own window; open projects come back at the next launch. Helix projects (.hlx) are plain JSON.

## Links

- [Website](https://www.helix-desktop.com/): overview, features and screenshots
- [FAQ](https://www.helix-desktop.com/faq/): requirements, privacy, statistical tests, exporting graphs, updates and support
- [Helix in numbers](https://www.helix-desktop.com/numbers/): installs and in-app updates per month, from GitHub’s public download counters (no tracker in the app)
- [Download](https://github.com/mickaphd/Helix/releases/latest): latest release, one DMG for Apple Silicon and one for Intel
- [Source code](https://github.com/mickaphd/Helix): GitHub repository and README
- [File format](https://github.com/mickaphd/Helix/blob/main/FILE-FORMAT.md): description of .hlx projects
- [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24156418): permanent Zenodo DOI to cite Helix, always pointing to the latest version
- [Discussions](https://github.com/mickaphd/Helix/discussions): questions and ideas
- [Issues](https://github.com/mickaphd/Helix/issues): bug reports
